title: What Happens If You Hold In a Sneeze?
description:
Send this to the friend who swallows every sneeze.
In a 2018 BMJ Case Reports case, a 34-year-old man blocked his nose and mouth to stop a forceful sneeze and tore a hole in the back of his throat. Air leaked into his neck and chest (doctors heard crackling down to his ribcage), he was tube-fed with IV antibiotics, spent seven days in hospital and had no further problems at two months. The authors call it rare but say blocking your nose and mouth during a sneeze is a dangerous manoeuvre. Cleveland Clinic adds that a stifled sneeze can also hurt your ears, and advises letting it out into a tissue or your elbow.
